Executive Overview

Trajectory Summary

From 1972-06-01 to 2026-03-11, AXP’s closing price increased from $1.22 to $305.99 (24,894.9% cumulative price return). The dividend-reinvested total return index implies a cumulative total return of 183,410.8% over the same window.

The long-run experience is dominated by a small number of large drawdown episodes (most notably the 2007–2009 decline) and long compounding phases. Investors evaluating AXP’s role in a portfolio should weigh a high long-run growth rate against deep cyclicality.

Key takeaway
AXP’s long-term return profile is strong, but the historical risk profile includes an ~84% peak-to-trough drawdown on Close.

Data Integrity & Scope

Source: /app/benchmark/data.csv (daily rows). Fields used: Date, Close, Volume, Dividends, Stock Splits.

Coverage: 13,556 trading days from 1972 through early 2026. Early 1970s volume is often 0 (documented in source brief), so volume conclusions emphasize periods with non-zero volume data.

All numeric values shown are computed directly from the dataset; no external prices, benchmarks, or inflation adjustments are used.

Bull/Bear Phases (Rule-Based)

Method: Bear phase starts on a ≥20% drawdown from a running peak; bull phase starts on a ≥25% rebound from a running trough. This is a transparent heuristic for regime segmentation (not an economic claim).

Appendix: Method Notes

  • Daily returns: Close(t)/Close(t−1) − 1.
  • Annualized volatility: Std(daily returns) × √252.
  • Drawdown: (cumulative return index / running max) − 1.
  • Total return index (TRI): TRI(t)=TRI(t−1)×(Close(t)+Dividends(t))/Close(t−1).
  • Calendar-year returns: last Close in year / first Close in year − 1.
